reason: Attacked on four fronts and it held on all four. WORDING: I did not trust the verifier's reading of the page, I downloaded Project Gutenberg ebook 10732, 209,841 bytes, whose title page reads THE ESSAYS OF ARTHUR SCHOPENHAUER: STUDIES IN PESSIMISM, Translated By T. Bailey Saunders, and stripped the markup. The text reads Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world. This is an error of the intellect as inevitable as that error of the eye which lets us fancy that on the horizon heaven and earth meet. That is the proposal character for character, terminal stop included, and the corroborating next sentence is there as claimed. Nothing is spliced: the quotation begins where the source's sentence begins and ends where it ends, and the paragraph before it, about Shakespeare and the tragic, is left off cleanly. LOCATOR: the contents list of the same file prints FURTHER PSYCHOLOGICAL OBSERVATIONS as one of the nine essays, and the sentence sits inside it, so the essay named on the card is the essay the sentence is in. The translator's own NOTE at the front confirms the rest of the citation in his own words: the essays here presented form a further selection from Schopenhauer's Parerga, brought together under a title which is not to be found in the original. That is the one thing worth flagging about the work and the card does not overclaim it. DATE: this was my best line of attack, because Saunders's Schopenhauer series runs from 1889 to 1897 and Studies in Pessimism is often catalogued 1891. It is not the 1891 volume. The first edition is November 1890, the second November 1891, then 1893, 1897, 1900, 1903, 1906, 1908 and 1913, so the year on the card is the year of the translation's first publication, exactly what rule 4 asks for. The card names no publisher, which is the honest form, since the imprint moved from Swan Sonnenschein to George Allen across those printings. ATTRIBUTION AND EVERYTHING ELSE: Schopenhauer's own prose in his own book, not reported and not a character, so no speaker is owed, and the misattribution list carries no Schopenhauer trap. shipped.js returns no shipped hit and no near-hit, puts him at 1 of 3 for the year from February, and reports him not banned and not at cap; carry.json holds no Schopenhauer at all and no second Schopenhauer appears anywhere in June's verdicts, so rule 8 is safe in both directions. Scope is clean: 1851 in German, 1890 in English, philosophy, not scripture, not oratory, not business writing, nothing needing a warning. The theme fit is as good as the month will get, since the sentence is about the eye mistaking its own horizon for the world's edge, which is June's ground, and it is cool rather than bleak despite the title of the volume it sits in. Source line form: leads with Arthur Schopenhauer, no dash of any kind, no straight double quote, 111 characters. I could not break it.

residual: One judgement call I decided not to refute on. Studies in Pessimism is subtitled A Series of Essays and Saunders's own note calls it a selection of essays from the Parerga, so Essay is arguable as the form, and the track already tags Bacon, Montaigne, Hume, Wilde and Stevenson that way. Philosophy is defensible too and is what February used for Schopenhauer's The Basis of Morality, so the tag is consistent within the person if not within the form. The editor may want to switch it to Essay, which would also help the philosophy lane's floor of two; the line itself does not depend on the answer.
